## Appearance

Faith is a tomboyish beauty who is as inspiring and original as she is pretty. She features golden-brown eyes, crimson cheeks, and a head of splendid, golden-brown curls.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P29](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0029), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P6](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0006), [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. THE GOOD-CONDUCT CLUB P0](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XXVI. MISS CORNELIA GETS A NEW POINT OF VIEW P22](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0022)_

## Personality

Faith Meredith is an eleven-year-old tomboy known for her remarkable beauty, joyous nature, and original character. Though inspiring, she is heedless and impulsive, frequently finding herself getting into scrapes. Possessing a proud streak, she refuses to play second fiddle to anyone, and she is steadfastly determined never to marry a minister.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P29](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0029), [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P31](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0031), [v5 CHAPTER V. ## History

Faith moved from [Maywater](../codex/places.md#maywater) to [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary with her widowed father, Mr. Meredith, and her siblings. Early on, she and her brothers and sister befriended the neighboring [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) children in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) and sheltered a runaway orphan, [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md), in their garret before Mary was adopted by a local woman. Faith frequently took impulsive actions to protect her family; after accidentally causing a scandal by cleaning house on a Sunday due to a mix-up in days, she publicly addressed the church congregation to clear her father's name. Soon after, upon learning that the church might lose crucial financial support, Faith boldly confronted the gruff [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md), ultimately securing his church attendance and salary contributions. When a visiting minister ate her cherished pet rooster, [Adam](../character/adam.md), for dinner, Faith stood by in silent revenge as the man's coat-tails caught fire at the hearth, though she was later comforted over the bird's loss by [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md).

Following a string of missteps, Faith and her siblings formed a self-policing Good-[Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#conduct-club). When Faith gave away her good stockings and faced wearing ugly striped ones to church, she attempted to make herself sick by standing on an ice bank in the graveyard; when that failed, she went to service bare-legged, leading to widespread local gossip that she ultimately addressed by publishing an explanatory letter in the town paper. During a later club-mandated fast to punish themselves for another disruption, her sister [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) fainted at church, sparking public criticism of their upbringing. Despite these misadventures, Faith and her siblings continued playing in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), once mistaking a neighbor in the dark for a ghost and fleeing in panic. She eventually celebrated the news of her father's upcoming wedding to [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) alongside her family.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Stacy and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert P3](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXIV. ## Quotes

> "I hope the girls are nice. I don’t like most of the girls round here. Even the nice ones are poky. But the Blythe twins look jolly. I thought twins always looked alike, but they don’t. I think the red-haired one is the nicest."
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P25](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0025)

> “I’ve heard of Mrs. Ford,” broke in Faith. “Bertie Shakespeare Drew told me about her. She was married fourteen years to a dead man and then he came to life.”
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P57](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0057)

> “Oh, it’s got to go on now,” cried Faith. “It’s a matter of honour. Don’t you dare tell anyone, Una. If you do I’ll never tell you secrets again!”
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER XVII. A DOUBLE VICTORY P28](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0028)

> "I love birds. Only—would Aunt Martha’s cat eat it? It’s so tragic to have your pets eaten. I don’t think I could endure it a second time."
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P34](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0034)

> "Just as nice as Mrs. Blythe—but different. I felt as if I wanted to hug her. She did hug me—such a nice, velvety hug. And she called me ‘dearest.’ It thrilled me. I could tell her anything."
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P40](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0040)
